== Biography ==
William Glasgow was born on 11 February 1811 in County Tyrone, Ireland, a son of [[Glasgow-1968|John Glasgow]] and [[Unknown-764117|Jane]].<ref name="HillsdaleWilliam">''Portrait and Biographical Album of Hillsdale County, Michigan'' (Chicago: Chapman Brothers, 1888), [https://archive.org/details/portraitbiograph00chpm/page/395/mode/1up p. 395]; [https://www.migenweb.org/hillsdale/bios/bios-g.html transcription].</ref>

The 1888 biography names seven children in John and Jane's family: Robert, Mary A., William, [[Glasgow-1967|John B. Glasgow Jr.]], Bessie, James and Margaret. William was the third child. The same account says his parents were County Tyrone natives of Scottish parentage, while John Jr.'s sketch describes them as Scottish-born and says they moved to County Tyrone after marriage.<ref name="HillsdaleWilliam" /><ref name="HillsdaleJohn">''Portrait and Biographical Album of Hillsdale County, Michigan'' (Chicago: Chapman Brothers, 1888), [https://archive.org/details/portraitbiograph00chpm/page/688/mode/1up p. 688]; [https://www.migenweb.org/hillsdale/bios/bios-g.html transcription].</ref>

William emigrated to the United States as a young man and lived at Auburn, New York, for about ten years. He married [[Glasgow-4025|Eliza Glasgow]], also born in County Tyrone, at Auburn on 4 August 1836. Although husband and wife shared the Glasgow surname, the biography describes them as members of different families. Eliza had emigrated with two brothers when she was about eighteen.<ref name="HillsdaleWilliam" />

In 1842 William, Eliza, their first child and William's brother John moved from Auburn to Fayette Township, Hillsdale County, Michigan. William and Eliza had four named children:

William died on 25 November 1897 at Jonesville, Hillsdale County, Michigan.<ref>{{FindAGrave|46450415}}</ref><ref>[https://www.myheritage.com/research/record-20538-2737844/william-glasgow-in-michigan-deaths Michigan deaths index entry for William Glasgow].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1968]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The 1888 Hillsdale biographical sketch places William, born11 February 1811, as the third of John and Jane’s seven children. That particular family list and exact date identify the selected John household. Conflicts elsewhere about parental origin or migration do not contradict William’s named place in the family.

Confident98%; secondary biographical family list, with origin and migration claims retained separately.

Next useful test: Compare the sibling sketches without transferring their migration conflicts into this parent pair.

Source basis already held: [https://archive.org/details/portraitbiograph00chpm/page/395/mode/1up Portrait and Biographical Album of Hillsdale County, Michigan (Chicago: Chapman Brothers, 1888), p. 395 (https://archive.org/details/portraitbiograph00chpm/page/395/mode/1up); transcription (https://www.migenweb.org/hillsdale/bios/bios-g.html).]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



The 1879 county history also discusses this family on page 263.<ref>''History of Hillsdale County, Michigan'' (Philadelphia: Everts & Abbott, 1879), [https://archive.org/details/bad0928.0001.001.umich.edu/page/263/mode/1up p. 263].</ref>

The 1888 sketches conflict on John and Jane's birthplaces and on whether the parents reached Hillsdale County in 1844 or 1848. Those discrepancies do not affect the independently consistent identification of William and John Jr. as their sons.

Eliza's two immigrant brothers remain unidentified. [[Glasgow-1171|Robert Glasgow]], born about 1809 in County Tyrone and later living in Cayuga County, is a plausible candidate for one brother, but no source presently proves the relationship.
